You may be wondering how to find the right adviser and what they will need from you. We can introduce you to a financial adviser near you who deals with divorce finances, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a divorce financial advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people in this situation want clear, local help with the money questions that come with separation.
needs: You need to understand how your pensions will be divided, especially if one pension is much larger than the other.
You want to know whether you can afford to stay in the family home or need to plan for a move.
You are unsure how to budget for life after divorce and want help with future income planning.
You have been offered a settlement and want an adviser to check it is fair before you agree.
You want to find a financial adviser near you who can work alongside your solicitor on the financial disclosure.
context_heading: What to understand about divorce financial advice
context: Divorce financial advisers help separating couples understand assets, pensions and future income, often alongside solicitors. Pensions are often the largest asset, and pension sharing orders need expert input. A local adviser can help you see the whole picture before you make decisions.

Financial advice in the UK is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Check that any adviser or firm is authorised, or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm, on the FCA register. Advisers must tell you whether their advice is independent or restricted, and how they charge.

faqs.q: Do I need a financial adviser if I already have a solicitor?
faqs.a: A solicitor handles the legal process, but a financial adviser can help with the detailed financial analysis, especially pensions and future income. They often work together to ensure the settlement is fair and workable.

faqs.q: How do I find a divorce financial advisor near me?
faqs.a: You can search online or ask your solicitor for recommendations. iComply can introduce you to a financial adviser in your area who deals with divorce finances, and they will quote you directly.

faqs.q: What is a pension sharing order and why does it need expert input?
faqs.a: A pension sharing order is a court order that splits a pension between divorcing couples. Pensions are often the largest asset, so expert input is needed to value them correctly and decide how to divide them fairly.

faqs.q: Can a financial adviser help me budget for life after divorce?
faqs.a: Yes, a divorce financial adviser can help you plan your future income and budget based on the settlement you receive. They can also help you understand the tax implications and how to manage your finances going forward.

extra_heading: What to expect at your first meeting with a divorce financial adviser
extra: At a first meeting, a divorce financial adviser will usually ask about your circumstances: your assets, pensions, income and what you hope to achieve from the divorce. They may also ask about your solicitor or mediator and whether any financial disclosure has been prepared. This helps them understand how they can help and whether they are the right fit for your needs.

You should expect the adviser to explain how they charge, whether their advice is independent or restricted, and what they can and cannot do. They may outline the steps involved in analysing your finances and how they would work with your solicitor. This is also your chance to ask about their experience with pension sharing orders and divorce settlements.

It is a good idea to bring any documents you have, such as pension statements, a list of assets, and any correspondence from your solicitor. The adviser can then give you a clearer picture of what needs to be done next. Remember that the adviser will quote you directly for their services, so you can decide whether to proceed.

extra_faqs.q: How is a divorce financial adviser different from a solicitor?
extra_faqs.a: A solicitor handles the legal aspects of divorce, such as filing papers and negotiating a settlement. A financial adviser focuses on the financial analysis, especially pensions and future income, and often works alongside your solicitor to ensure the settlement is fair and workable.

extra_faqs.q: Can a divorce financial adviser help if we are not yet divorced?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, many people seek financial advice early in the separation process to understand their options. An adviser can help you prepare for financial disclosure and consider how assets might be divided, even before the divorce is finalised.

extra_faqs.q: Will I have to pay for the first meeting?
extra_faqs.a: Some advisers offer a free initial consultation, while others charge for their time. You should ask about fees upfront and get a written quote before proceeding. iComply introduces you to an adviser who will quote you directly.
